sections.label: Clause 6 amends NPF Act
sections.summary: Clause 6 amends the NPF Act to extend the PFAB's specific powers to investment promotion activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill amends the NPF Act to extend specific powers of the Productivity Fund Administration Board (PFAB), which administers the NPF, to also cover investment promotion activities.

sections.label: NPF top-up and scope expansion
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance announced a $4 billion NPF top-up and expansion to include investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To demonstrate our commitment to attracting new investments, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance announced in the FY2023 Budget Statement that the Government will top up the National Productivity Fund (NPF) with $4 billion and expand the scope of the Fund to include investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sections.label: CPCF, NPF support and expansion
sections.summary: The CPCF has helped over 10,000 companies, mostly SMEs, and the NPF supports initiatives like the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To date, the CPCF has helped over 10,000 companies, with more than 90% being SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The NPF supports initiatives, such as the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programme, which has helped more than 7,000 fresh ITE and polytechnic graduates deepen their skills through integrating on-the-job training with classroom learning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: With the proposed expansion, we will also be able to tap on the NPF to anchor quality investments from MNEs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This includes the use of incentives to attract companies in advanced industries to make new manufacturing investments here.

sections.label: Budget 2023 NPF announcement welcomed
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's 2023 Budget announcement of the $4 billion NPF top-up and scope expansion was welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In his 2023 Budget speech, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s announcement of the $4 billion top up to our NPF and the expansion of the scope of NPF to include investment promotion was very much welcomed.

sections.label: Intel Germany plant subsidies comparison
sections.summary: Intel has sealed an agreement to build a $33 billion semiconductor plant in Magdeburg, Germany, with US$11 billion in German subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If we were to compare with other state support abroad, Intel has sealed an agreement to build a new $33 billion semiconductor plant in Magdeburg, Germany, with US$11 billion in subsidies from Germany.

sections.label: NPF disbursements over five years
sections.summary: Low Yen Ling said the NPF disbursed over S$1 billion across 47 Government projects in five years, half for productivity and half for CET.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On 2 March 2023, Minister of State Low Yen Ling mentioned that over the last five years, Singapore’s NPF has disbursed more than S$1 billion across 47 Government projects related to productivity improvements and continuing education and training (CET) and about half was spent on productivity projects and the other half on CET programmes.

sections.label: IRAS productivity funds cheating sentence
sections.summary: Lim Chit Foo was sentenced in March 2022 to nine years and four months' jail for cheating IRAS into disbursing over $11.8 million in productivity funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In March 2022, Lim Chit Foo was sentenced to nine years and four months' jail for cheating the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) into disbursing more than $11.8 million in productivity funds.

sections.label: NPF top-up and ITM growth
sections.summary: The passage asks how a robust system can fund innovation without stifling it while ensuring governance, and notes Minister Gan Kim Yong's cited ITM growth figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we top up our NPF with an additional $4 billion dollars, how do we also ensure that we have a robust system that balances the pace required to fund innovation and not stifle it while ensuring good governance?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: During the Committee of Supply debate in 2023, Minister Gan Kim Yong highlighted notable progress within the 23 ITM sectors, showcasing a 3.5% annual growth in value added (VA) from 2016 to 2019, surpassing the overall economy's 3.1% average.

sections.label: Fund expansion and grant clauses
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong proposed expanding the Fund by $4 billion, with clause 3(b) allowing grants for investments or economic activities in Singapore and clause 6 recognising investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In that speech, Deputy Prime Minister Wong also proposed an expansion of the Fund, by $4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 3(b) allows grants to now be directed towards the general purpose of "making investments in Singapore… or carrying out economic activities in Singapore, in order to develop the Singapore economy." Similarly, clause 6 amends the Second Schedule to recognise investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sections.label: ChatGPT rapid user growth
sections.summary: ChatGPT became pervasive at a rabid speed, amassing its user base in a mere five days.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: ChatGPT has become pervasive at a rabid speed, having amassed that user base in a mere five days.

sections.label: AI automating routine and cognitive work
sections.summary: Five years ago routine mental work could be automated, but AI can now outperform white-collar workers in creative, cognitively-demanding, non-routine tasks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Five years ago, we had already seen examples of how routine mental work, such as data entry, insurance underwriting, tax preparation and telemarketing, could be easily automated away.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But AI can now outperform even white-collar workers engaged in creative, cognitively-demanding, non-routine tasks, such as designing websites, performing radiographic diagnoses and summarising legal briefs.

sections.label: Jobs in 2018 versus 1940
sections.summary: Close to three-fifths of jobs in 2018 did not exist in 1940.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Close to three-fifths of jobs in 2018 did not exist in 1940.

sections.label: Companies failing to deploy AI
sections.summary: Companies that fail to deploy AI extensively will be left behind by competitors or industry obsolescence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Eventually, companies that fail to deploy AI extensively in their business operations will be left behind, either by competitors who are better able to do so, or because AI will have rendered their entire industry obsolete.

sections.label: National AI Strategy productivity mentions
sections.summary: The National AI Strategy mentions productivity a dozen times but offers only three concrete examples of potential gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The National AI Strategy document appears to recognise this but it is noteworthy that the term "productivity" only appears a dozen times in the 45-page document and twice in the foreword and twice in quotes, leaving the body of the document offering only three concrete examples for potential productivity gains from AI.

sections.label: NPF in-depth report to Parliament
sections.summary: The NPF could commit to an in-depth report to Parliament detailing use of $4 billion, activities, beneficiaries, and SkillsFuture overlap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What may be even better is if the NPF will commit to providing an in-depth report to Parliament that details how precisely the $4 billion in funds are to be used – the sort of activities these funds support and the main beneficiaries of these programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will provide greater clarity on how channelled funds, with Government bodies as an intermediary, ultimately get to our businesses and workers to upgrade their productivity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It will also clarify how, if at all, monies from the fund may overlap with those set aside for SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Budget 2023 NPF top-up
sections.summary: Budget 2023 provided a $4 billion top-up and included investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Budget 2023, a $4 billion top-up was provided and investment promotion was included as a supportable activity.

sections.label: NPF disbursements over five years
sections.summary: Over five years the NPF disbursed over $1 billion across 47 Government projects, with about half for CET.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As reported by the Minister of State for the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) Low Yen Ling in Parliament on 2 March 2023, over the past five years, Singapore's NPF has disbursed more than $1 billion across 47 Government projects related to productivity improvements and continuing education and training (CET).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: About half of the funds from the NPF are allocated to CET programmes.

sections.label: Addressing concerns on fund utilisation
sections.summary: Addressing the concerns raised can ensure funds are effectively utilised to benefit employers and employees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By addressing the concerns raised, I believe we can ensure that the funds are effectively utilised to benefit both employers and employees.

sections.label: NPF top-up adequacy question
sections.summary: Mr Sharael Taha asked whether the $4 billion top-up is adequate and how NPF funding can be balanced across productivity enhancement, CET and investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha asked if the $4 billion top-up is adequate and how we can balance the use of NPF funding across the three purposes of productivity enhancement, CET and investment promotion.

sections.label: Expanding NPF to investment promotion
sections.summary: The NPF is being expanded to cover investment promotion so additional firepower is ready to attract key investments when opportunities do not match existing funding mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The reason we are expanding the NPF to cover investment promotion is to ensure that we have the additional firepower ready to attract key investments to Singapore in the event that the timing of these opportunities does not neatly match with existing funding mechanisms bound by the terms of Government.

sections.label: Selecting projects and sectors
sections.summary: Economic agencies must select projects bringing value and critical capabilities, using NPF funds to anchor quality investments in advanced manufacturing, green economy and digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our economic agencies have to carefully select the right projects that bring value and critical capabilities to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will use the NPF funds to anchor quality investments from best-in-class companies in high-growth and high value-added sectors, including advanced manufacturing, the green economy and digital economy.

sections.label: Labour productivity growth since 2010
sections.summary: Since the NPF was set up in 2010, Singapore met the Economic Strategies Committee's 2% to 3% labour productivity growth target, with 2.9% growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Since the NPF was set up in 2010, Singapore has met the labour productivity growth target set by the Economic Strategies Committee of 2% to 3% per annum over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: At the aggregate level, our labour productivity growth rate over this period was 2.9%, which was higher than most advanced economies, such as the US, Germany, Switzerland and Japan, over the same period.

sections.label: Bill expands NPF Act scope
sections.summary: The proposed amendments in this Bill seek to expand the scope of the NPF Act to cover investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proposed amendments in this Bill seek to expand the scope of the NPF Act to cover investment promotion.

sections.label: Broad drafting and stated focus
sections.summary: The Bill's language is kept broad for future changes, while the Second Reading speech states the focus and intent publicly on record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The drafting of the Bill to keep the language broad is to cater for future changes because we cannot predict what are the new industries that will emerge; what are the new activities that we will need to focus on; what are some of the new investments that we want to attract to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But the purpose of me in my Second Reading opening speech making it clear what is the focus and the intent is so that we provide clarity publicly and on record that this is what NPF wants to focus on.

sections.label: Singapore productivity and investment
sections.summary: Poor total factor or labour productivity would prevent Singapore from attracting investments, providing good jobs and real wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If it is true that over the years, Singapore's total factor productivity (TFP) or labour productivity has been very poor, I do not think it will be possible for Singapore, as a very open small economy, to be able to attract investments, to be able to provide good jobs for people, and for our workers to be able to see, over time, real wage increases.
